Shabbo Bi vs Ganeshram on 4 November, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:32038
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 4 th Of November, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 999 of 2018
 Shabbo Bi And Others
 Versus
 Ganeshram And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Akhil Godha, learned counsel for the appellants.

Shri Nitin Singh Bhati, learned counsel for responden  Shri Akshansh Mehra appearing on behalf of Sanjay Kum  learned counsel for respondent No.3.
 ORDER

The appellants have filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 11.11.2017 passed by the learned Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandsaur (M.P.) in MACC No.119/2017, whereby they are challenging the quantum of compensation on the ground of incorrect assessment of the income of the deceased.
2. The liability of the Insurance Company is not under dispute.
3. The brief facts of the case are that on 12.07.2016 at around 7:40 PM, Rashid Shah was riding his motorcycle.

When he reached near the Reliance Petrol Pump on Mhow-Neemuch Road, Mandsaur,
respondent No.1 was driving a pick-up vehicle bearing registration number MP-14-GB-1066 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32038 2 MA-999-2018 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of the Rashid, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
He was rushed to District Hospital, Mandsaur, and after receiving primary treatment, he was referred to Maharana Bhupal Rajkiya Hospital, Udaipur, where he was declared dead by the doctors.
3.1 The appellants / claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Rashid.

The Claims Tribunal after recording evidence concluded that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle,
which resulted in Rashid's death.
Consequently, the Claims Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,37,000/- to the appellants.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Claims Tribunal while considering the income of the deceased Rashid has discarded the claim that he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month,
although Ex.16, a licence for running a hotel was exhibited before the Tribunal.

Apart from this, Ex.
P-17, a document evidencing the continuation of the restaurant licence, was also placed on record.
4.1 He submits that the wife of the deceased also stated in her deposition before the Court that the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- per month from other businesses as well.

However, the Tribunal while considering Exs. P-16 and P-17 observed that the hotel is situated near the cremation ground,
thus, the income was disbelieved.
Learned counsel argues that this could not have been a valid basis for discarding the clear evidence regarding income.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32038 3 MA-999-2018 4.2
He further submits that the wife of the deceased Shabbo Bi (AW- 1) clearly deposed before the Tribunal that the deceased was also engaged in the business of selling sand and boulders.
However, the Claims Tribunal without any basis, has discarded this evidence and assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month.

Learned counsel submits that even if the income of the deceased were to be considered on the basis of the minimum wages prescribed for a semi-skilled labourer, it could not have been less than Rs.7,760/- per month, which was the minimum wages for unskilled labourer at the relevant time.

4.3 Apart from this, he submits that nothing has been added under the head of future prospects,
although the deceased was 45 years old at the time of his death.
Furthermore, no amount of compensation under the head of loss of consortium has been awarded, even though the claimants are the widow and three sons of the deceased.
He therefore prays for enhancement of the compensation.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the claimants/appellants have completely failed to bring any document on record regarding the business of the deceased in selling sand and boulders.
Apart from this, although Exs. P-16 and P-17, which are licences for running a hotel were produced, no document regarding the income from the said hotel has been brought on record.
This goes to show that although the licence was obtained the hotel was never actually operated.
He therefore prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 reiterates the arguments NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:32038 4 MA-999-2018 advanced by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

7. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
8.
From perusal of Ex. P-16, it is clear that in the year 2011, the deceased Rashid was granted a licence for running a hotel.

Shabbo Bi (AW- Shabbo Bi vs Ganeshram on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69039310/
2 1), the wife of the deceased deposed that he was operating a hotel in the name of "Maa Ka Ashirwad".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Other witnesses corroborated the same.
9. However, during the cross examination of Mumtaz (AW-4), it was revealed that no documents regarding the business of the deceased have been brought on record.
It is thus seen that apart from the licence, there is no evidence to show that the deceased was actively running a particular business and earning income.
10. Nevertheless, the existence of the hotel licence cannot be ignored.
In the considered view of this Court, the average income between a skilled and unskilled labourer should be taken into account, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case.
Considering the minimum wages for these two categories, the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.7,000/- per month.
11. The deceased was 45 years of age.
Accordingly, a 25% addition has been made to his income under the head of future prospects.
Considering that the claimants are the widow and three sons of the deceased, Rs.40,000/- each is awarded to the four of them under the head of loss of consortium.

12. In view of the above additions and modifications to the income of the deceased, the total c o m p e n s a t i o n n o w c o m e s t o R s . 1 1 , 7 0 , 0 0 0 / - . A f t e r N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

2025:MPHC-IND:32038 5 MA-999-2018 deducting the amount already awarded of Rs.6,37,000/-,
the enhance amount of Rs.5,33,000/- is to be paid to the appellants/claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal.
13. It is seen from the record that the appeal has been valued at Rs.4,00,000/-.

The appellants /
claimants are directed to pay the deficit Court fee within 4 weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
If they fail to pay the remaining Court fees within this period, the enhanced amount shall cease to carry any interest.
14. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Anushree Shabbo Bi vs Ganeshram on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69039310/
